Newcastle free-kick for a trip on Willock. Hall takes and Leeds head it out for a throw-in.

Livramento improves the quality of crosses with two that at least find the middle of the box even if they were headed away by Elvedi and Justin respectively.

Newcastle are enjoying more possession but the crossing has been awful when they do get down the flanks, Touré the latest offender.

Barnes shoots down Trafford’s throat. Barnes had thrown himself down in the box moments earlier and there was a VAR check but there was nothing like the contact required to send him swan-diving on to the grass.

Wissa gets down the right and whips over a low cross but Willock’s touch was too heavy.

There was a piece in the Athletic today saying Newcastle pivoted to Hornicek instead of pursuing Trafford again because he had a very high ceiling and was younger. He hasn’t caught much here, dropping the ball even when he chooses not to punch.

Matthias Jaissle promised high intensity, high octane, front foot football when he was interviewed for the Newcastle job. He and sporting director Ross Wilson have repeated that promise several times since he was appointed. There has been no sign of it since the opening weekend against Liverpool.

Newcastle are passive, they look disorganised in midfield and weak at the back. Oh and they barely apply pressure let alone attack dangerously.

These are early days but this performance and result had been coming. A pretty brutal reality check after all the positive noise and bold predictions in pre-season. This defeat will drop Newcastle to 12th in the table, where they finished last season under Eddie Howe.

Leeds 4 Newcastle 0 (Okafor) Ampadu hurls it into the box. A defender heads it to the edge of the area where Okafor thumps a left-footed half-volley in off the right post.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x

Livramento slides in to stop Okafor’s drive down the left, giving Leeds another opportunity to throw it long.

Triple change: Livramento → DedicTouré → Fernandez-PardoWillock → Murphy

Leeds catch Newcastle playing short from the back. Stach blindsides Steur 20 yards out, tackles him, cuts inside then bends a left foot shot into the side-netting.

After Hall stings Trafford’s palms with a strike from distance. Newcastle want a penalty when the ball hits Tanaka’s arm … but it was outside the area and then Murphy, in frustration, chops down Gudmundsson and takes the booking as an occupational hazard.

Elvedi sloppily gives the ball way to Wissa who tries to set Fernandez-Pardo through down the left. Justin sticks with him and Bogle mops up after Justin was tripped.

Gudmundsson does the upended beetle when he tries to break from the corner and collides with a Newcastle player. He claims he was fouled and wthrashes about like a RL player after he’s tackled. He continues to do a Rumpelstiltskin polka of peevishness towards the ref for a while.

Newcastle corner on the left that Trafford backpedals to tip behind for another.

No changes at half-time for Newcastle as they kick off. Leeds break through the middle quickly and Calvert-Lewin seems to push the ball past Botman and shapes to shoot before Steur slides in with a crucial tackle just inside the box.

The first goal is now an own goal. The explanation is that Tanaka’s shot was on target but the deflection from Steur meant it was going wide until it hit Miley.

Now the second goal has been credited to Bogle as Calvert-Lewin’s header struck the top of his head before it went in.

You could not say that this scoreline is undeserved. Newcastle are being demolished physically. The central midfield two – Steur and Miley – just don’t have the power to screen their defence.

Leeds 3 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Leeds are running all over Newcastle who seem physically flimsy. Calvert-Lewin chops in from the left on to a flick-on, the ball takes a deflection off the Newcastle captain and he steers it into the far corner with a right-foot shot.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9

Calvert-Lewin is booked for catching Botman in the face with a straight arm rather than a swinging arm. ‘Reckless but not violent.’ Trafford had punchd the corner away at the back post to set Leeds off on a counter.

Tanaka gives the ball away carelessly in midfield and Newcastle work it to Wissa who chops inside past Elvedi, hangs out his own leg looking for contact and hits the deck. The ref waves play on and the ball runs to Barnes in the left of the area. He shapes to shoot but Muharemovic sprinted over to make a fine block-tackle, forcing it behind for a corner.

Newcastle are rocking here. They cannot win a tackle.

For those of us who have watched all Newcastle United’s games this season, this was coming. They do not have any consistent attacking threat, they do no create chances and they are not secure at the back either.

They’ve survived by converting the very few chances they create in games but they have not even had a shot in the first half here.

Leeds should be three up after Hornicek fumbled Gudmundsson’s shot from the left. The ball falls to Calvert-Lewin five yards out and he triesto dink it over the keeper who recovers well to smother it.

Leeds 2 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Newcastle try to play the ball out from the back, give it away cheaply to Bogle who feeds Justin haring down the right. He is ostensibly the right centre-back but he is a full-back by trade and stands up a perfect near-post cross that Calvert-Lewin hangs in the air to bury with the firmest of headers. In fact it transpires that his downward header struck Bogle and another deflection benefits rampant Leeds –162 seconds between the goals.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj

Leeds 1 Newcastle 0 (Tanaka) Good move, spawny finish. Tanaka sprays a pass out to Okafor who drives at Dedic then picks out Tanaka who had held his run. He cushions the pass then lets fly. The ball hits Steur, deflects on to Miley and then loops into the right of the goal with Hornicek understandably stranded.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO

Good tackle by Steur on Bogle stops the Leeds right-back flying forward after Calvert-Lewin’s flick-on.

Newcastle really are not afraid to launch the ball forward are they? Football tactics are constantly evolving and fashions come back around. What better way to play through a press than to bypass the midfield completely? The hope is it will also cause the centre-backs problems, get them facing their own goal under pressure from one of Newcastle’s rapid forward players in a foot race.

It almost worked a couple of times in the first half but it should be pointed out that the best direct/long ball teams of the past tended to have a striker who was dominant in the air. Newcastle do not currently have one which does limit their threat from flick ons.

Newcastle break from defending a long throw. Wissa carries it 60 yards but with Murphy and Fernadez-Pardo better placed, he tries to shoot from 25 yards and plinks it straight at Trafford, provoking an inevitable ‘Woooooooo’.

From the resulting long throw Elvedi is found at the back post, unmarked and attempts to volley it towards goal, missing the ball entirely. It was so wild that even the Leeds staff laugh at how inept it was.

Leeds have a corner when they use one of their signature moves, Bogle cutting in from the right across the back four to take a ball over the top. He controls it but cannot force it past Thiaw.

Hornicek claws out the corner to Bogle 18 yards out. He puts his laces through a volley that Hornicek parries up high and punches away when he has a second go.

Newcastle chip it long again, this time down the right. Gudmundsson holds off Murphy and Leeds will have the relief of a goal-kick.

Leeds are finding it hard now to play through Newcastle’s high press and the intensity with which they are hounding keeper and defenders.

Newcastle keep looking to use their pace with balls over the top for Wissa, Murphy and Fernandez-Pardo. Wissa closes Trafford down quickly again. He needs to release it with more urgency.

Gonzalez hs not recovered from being struck on the head by the ball and is being replaced by Steur as a concussion sub.

Justin heads over his own bar when Newcastle chip a long pass down the inside right. Wissa beats Muharemovic and tries to find Fernandez-Pardo but Justin got there first. Newcastle go short from the corner and Leeds force them back into their own half.

Terrific save from Hornicek down low to his right. Tanaka’s cross from the left found Justin creeping round the back on the right and heading across goal from the back post. Bogle swivelled and tried a sidewinder flick that was arrowing towards the bottom left corner until the keeper swooped to turn it away with his right hand.

Wissa is ticking, feeling he is getting nothing from the referee when challenging for the ball, the latest incident involving a collision with Justin which was 50-50.

Leeds have been the slicker of the two sides, their passing and movement causing the full-backs problems. Okafor dribbles down the left and centres. Stach lays it back to Ampadu who hammers a half-volley from 18 yards that poleaxes Calvert-Lewin who was in an offside position.

Newcastle fans sing ‘There’s only one Kevin Keegan’ as the visitors’ defence sweeps the ball around. When they knock the ball up the inisde-right channel Wissa is penalised for swinging his arm and catching Muharemovic in the mooey.

Wissa presses Trafford high and the goalkeeper is a bit too casual but gets away with it. His clearance bounces off the attacker’s shin and loops out to the right. Leeds shift it quickly out to the left with Gudmundsson and Okafor bombing forward. A vicious cross from the left-back hits a Newcastle leg, loops up and smaxks Gonzales flush in the face, knocking him off his feet. The ref stops play.

Two bad moments for Newcastle early on. Lewis Hall caught out by a simple run and pass behind him and then, from the resulting corner Mathias Fernandez-Pardo looked very fortunate, in my opinion, to avoid conceding a penalty for handball.

He got the benefit of the doubt presumably because the ball bounced up onto his hand as he tried to bring it under control and he did not intend to control it with his hand or knock it away. The handball law confuses me but there is a higher threshold now.

Stach tackles Wissa in the centre-circle. Wissa is playing behind Fernandez-Pardo. Ampadu receives a long pass over the top, coming back from an offside position in the nick of time.

Fernandez-Pardo’s outstretched left arm is struck in the penalty area with the ball after they win the header but the ref waves play on and stops the game for a foul on the new striker.

It’s never a problem to come to Elland Road and the singing of Marching On Together before kick-off makes this one of the top three atmospheres in the country, easily. There are problems with VAR, though, and the whole stadium has just seen the ball strike Matias Fernanzes-Pardo’s hand in the area. The reason it is a problem is because we have become conditioned to thinking every time a ball touches someone on the arm in the area, a penalty should be awarded. It is preposterous that faceless beaks have distorted the game so much.

Leeds kick off, attacking the South Stand, from left to right, as they always prefer to do. Justin and Bogle combine on the right and Bogle bends a pass inside HAll to Stach who chooses to cross rather than shoot. It hits Botman and goes out for a corner.

Leeds are in their home kit of white with yellow and blue pinstripe hoops, Newcastle in their navy away kit.

Anthony [Elanga] is injured. Unfortunately we have to investigate further how long he will be out but obviously we miss him. We wish him to come back as quickly as possible. It could be [a long-term injury] but he will get another MRI next week and then we’ll see.

Lewis Hall is the perfect player profile for how we play. he is a young lad still and we are very excited [that he has signed a new contract].

The start was not easy. We didn’t have lots of time to prepare for pre-season and that’s one reason we are happy and satisfied with the start. But there is potential and we will work hard on the margins we want to improve.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

But Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

Jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

There are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

This is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

He formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the new boy Fernandez-Pardo?

Mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. And yet he was always gracious about Leeds and particularly fond of Don Revie. He was one of very few football people without a strong Leeds United connection who went to his funeral in 1989.

Apparently he was injured in training, the nature of the injury is unspecified.

Newcastle have made a very good start particularly in their transitional moments on the counter-attack. We have to be switched on today to get the next points.

After many years of suffering our supporters deserve it [high expectations]. It’s good but we are far away from not being humble. Our feet are on the ground. We know the second year is always difficult. We have made a good start and it is always important to ride the momentum as long as possible.

Eddie Howe has left a legacy and the culture he created is still around. Matthias has to work with it. They are unbeaten. they are very dangerous with many pacy players up front. It’s important not to lose the ball too easily and always be switched on against Newcastle.

Leeds United Trafford; Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Bogle, Ampadu, Tanaka, Gudmundsson; Stach, Okafor; Calvert-Lewin. Substitutes Zetterer, Bard, Bijol, Longstaff, Aaronson, Wilson, James, Bahoya, Nmecha.

Newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; González, L Miley; Murphy, Fernandez-Pardo, Barnes; Wissa. Substitutes Pope, Livramento, Schär, Bamba, Steur, Touré, Willock, Ramsey, M Miley.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

The architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. His two goals that night were his sixth and seventh against Leeds in eight matches for Leicester and the Toon. Back in the last century and at the turn of this one, Alan Shearer scored 21 league goals in 23 games against Leeds for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle, it can feel like one bogeyman passing the baton to another.

Newcastle’s sound form with their new model team this season has been based on searing pace and their ability on the counter whether with runners, in the case of Anthony Elanga, or with long diagonals against Tottenham that ripped a hole in the left side of their defence. Leeds rallied from being overrun by Brentford at half-time in their last home game to switch from three at the back to four and wrest back the initiative and while they reverted for the Brighton draw, in both games it was the introduction of Ao Tanaka in midfield that gave them control.

It is genuinely hard to decide whether the 6-3 defeat by Chelsea in the Carabao Cup from being 2-0 up at Stamford Bridge is significant to Leeds league form. One simplistic way of looking at it would be to say Leeds reserves were better than Chelsea’s reserves in the first half and Chelsea’s first-team were better than Leeds reserves and their shaky, debutant keeper in the second. But any similar defensive frailties tonight and there will be jitters over the next week before the international break. Newcastle, by contrast, toiled in their 1-0 victory over Millwall but the result glosses over a lack of incision for long spells of it.

Joe Rodon is out for Leeds for at least another month while Newcastle have changed to withholding information about their treatment room under Matthias Jaissle who says that it should be ‘confidential’. We do know that Joelinton, William Osula and Dan Burn are likely to still be out given the nature of their injuries but Amar Dedic, who came off at half-time at the New Den with a thigh or hamstring problem, may be back.

#1609. “If there can be a way out” – Moretto states Milan have no intention of offering Tomori a renewal

It seems we are heading into the final year of Fikayo Tomori’s playing relationship with AC Milan, with talk of a renewal silent.

Next year, at the end of June, Tomori’s deal expires and if nothing is done before then, his six-year spell with the club will come to an end.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s been an up-and-down season for the Englishman, especially after he was included in the ‘bomb squad’ through the mercato. However, he was needed back in the squad and reintegrated.

Despite showing this fight, though, it seems unlikely that he’ll be rewarded with a new deal. There are plans to invest heavily in the club next year and the defender isn’t seen as a pillar of the team, let alone the defence. So a renewal isn’t being focused on.

As Matteo Moretto told viewers on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, Tomori previously had a chance at a renewal. However, that now seems to have gone, as MilanNews relays.

“There’s a before and after regarding Tomori. In my opinion, if Massimiliano Allegri had remained on the Milan bench, perhaps in that case there could have been a chance of a renewal for Tomori.

“Then there was the slightly peculiar way Milan handled the Tomori situation. Tomori is a player who has always been absolutely professional and deeply loves the Milan shirt; he has always shown all his commitment.

“It’s true, he was sidelined; Milan tried to find solutions on the way out right in the last days of the transfer window. His contract expires in 2027.

“There were discussions underway for the renewal when Allegri was on the bench; then, with time and with the succession of certain events, this type of renewal was no longer discussed.

“To date, the negotiations are absolutely at a standstill. There is no dialogue between the parties and I repeat, Tomori’s contract expires in 2027.

“We’ll see if in January there can be a way out, perhaps with the payment of compensation to Milan, or if it will reach zero in June, but as of today there is no trace of a possible renewal.”

#1608. Liverpool transfer news: Who is Sidy Barhama Ndiaye, the 16-year-old Senegalese phenomenon expected in 2028?

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 13:28

Liverpool may have found their next great Senegalese talent. The Premier League club have reportedly reached a verbal agreement to sign Sidy Barhama Ndiaye, a 16-year-old winger who currently plays for Diambars.

However, Liverpool fans will have to be patient, as the young Senegalese cannot move to England until January 2028.

The news was revealed by Fabrizio Romano, who confirmed that a verbal agreement exists between the two parties.

Having already been given a trial by Liverpool in the summer of 2025, Ndiaye reportedly convinced the club's scouts, who have now secured an option on his arrival. Born on 31 December 2009, he will turn 18 at the end of 2027, which is a requirement for a move to England.

??? Liverpool have verbally agreed deal to sign 16 year old winger Sidy Barhama Ndiaye, here we go! Senegalese talent to join in January 2028, when he turns 18. Ndiaye was already at Liverpool on trial in 2025 and ready to become #LFC player for future. https://t.co/DrBIfNkPJR

A product of Diambars, one of the most renowned academies in Senegal, Sidy Barhama Ndiaye plays mainly on the right but can also operate on the left. He first caught the eye at the 2025 Under-17 Africa Cup of Nations, played when he was only 15, before continuing to progress with Senegal's youth teams.

His main qualities are his pace, his explosiveness and his ability to beat an opponent one on one. Very direct when receiving the ball, he likes to provoke, accelerate and create openings. He also has a degree of efficiency in the final ball, as he again demonstrated at the Under-17 World Cup.

During Senegal's 9-0 thrashing of Cuba, the young winger scored one goal and provided two assists. The performance helped to boost his reputation among European observers and scouts.

The comparison with Sadio Mane comes naturally around the young Senegalese.

Besides his origins, Ndiaye shares with his illustrious elder an attacking profile built on pace, penetration and the ability to make a difference on the wings. And if Liverpool, who benefited from Mane's talent for six seasons, complete the deal, that comparison will be unavoidable.

However, there is still a long way to go before he can be expected to play at Anfield. Between now and January 2028, Ndiaye will have to continue to progress at Diambars and confirm the promise shown with Senegal's youth teams.

Liverpool, for their part, have already taken a position on a player they want to integrate into their long-term project.

#1607. An Arseblog update

It’s around 10.30am on Friday, November 6th 2026. I’m in my hotel room in London, doing a few Arseblog bits on my laptop, and getting ready for the launch of the The 22 in the Big Red that night.

My phone rings. It’s a Dublin number but one not in my contacts. Typically I wouldn’t answer, but I think I know who it probably is. I’m right. It’s the Oncology department of the hospital I was admitted to a couple of weeks ago. They have news.

“Can you come into us on Monday afternoon at 2.30?”

“Great, we’ll see you then. Oh, and you should bring somebody with you. It’s a lot of information to take in.”

As of this moment, I’m still not 100% on all the details. I had another scan yesterday, and I have a procedure scheduled for Tuesday which will give us more information. However, they’ve already laid out a plan for three months of chemo, which is kind of why I’m writing this.

My very, very strong instinct with any medical stuff is to keep it private. And I suppose if I was a guy who had a regular 9 to 5 and went to the office every day, I could do that. However, the privilege of my work is that it is very public facing. I do the stuff, you read the stuff and listen to the stuff, and you are part of my life in a very big way; in the same way – even if it it’s just for a few minutes each morning, or a couple of hours in your headphones – that I’m part of yours.

Which isn’t say I feel like I owe anyone an explanation, but this is my reality now, and for what’s likely to be an arduous road ahead for a while. Unfortunately, that makes it part of your reality too. I will say, I’m not going to document my ‘journey’. Fair play to anyone who does. Whatever you need to do to get through the challenges an illness presents, it’s just not really who I am. I don’t even do video on podcasts about football, so I’m not gonna start now for something like this!

But I do need the distraction of work, of Arsenal, of football and all its ludicrousness and drama, and this incredible community that has grown over the near 25 years of Arseblog’s existence. I’ve missed it this week, despite the fact it’s been such a difficult time in this household. We’ve gone through all the normal human reactions and emotions, and the whole thing was compounded by the fact I came back from London with the single worst stomach bug I’ve ever had in my life. To be honest, that felt a bit mean from the universe. Here, have a bit of this, and just to make you feel worse, you will require about twenty visits to the bathroom every day. It’s a bit like one of those days where every set of traffic lights you hit turns red as you approach, but the traffic lights also make your arse hurt. Fuck off!

So, I’m going to be around, and I’m gonna do my best to do what I normally do. I need as much normal as I can get, because right now too much isn’t. But there will be days when I’m not, or I can’t be, and I’m happy to let the lads pick up the slack as much as possible. To preempt many messages and thoughts, I know what the priority is, and I’m not going to push myself at the expense of my health or getting better. I have a vested interest in, you know, making a full recovery. I’m not going to risk doing anything that might conflict with that.

But I also feel like the best way to navigate this is to not let it take over my life, or to define who I am. I’m still just an Irish bloke with a website about Arsenal first and foremost, and the last week or so has made me feel strangely protective of that. A dose of perspective is a really interesting thing, I know what the most important thing is right now, but that can only succeed if I remain myself. I hope that makes sense.

Some lads kicking a ball around a football pitch is, in the grand scheme of things, not that important. But hasn’t that always been the case? Football is so intrinsic to all of us, and we give so much of our time and energy to it, because we (well most of us) understand the absurdity of giving so much of ourselves to something that is completely out of our control. We can pretend otherwise, but that’s all part of the fun too. Lucky socks and lucky shirts and matchday routines. Our brain’s way of trying to make it feel like we have some influence, because we need that sliver of pretence, but in the end it’s about whether some millionaire at the back post can apply the finish.

I suppose at least this shit waited until there was an Interlull. Thanks for that.

I’m lucky because I have an amazing wife and daughter, and family and friends, who will be with me every step of the way. Their support thus far has been incredible, and I know I can count on it 100%. I’m going to listen to the doctors and the medical team and do whatever it is they ask of me. They seem to know what they’re on about, which is reassuring. Almost like they’re experts or something. We should listen to them.

I know as well that wider support from the Arseblog community will be forthcoming, and I just wanted to say in advance that I appreciate it hugely. I suspect that replying to every message is going to be beyond me, and in normal circumstances that would bother me greatly. I always try to respond to every email I get, even if it takes me a while, but in this instance I hope you’ll understand if I don’t or can’t.

So that’s where we are. I still don’t know where we’ll end up or how we’ll get there, but despite the fact I’m scared and worried, I’m also positive and determined. I could really do without this, to be quite honest, but it is what it is, and the only way through is forward. I’ll keep you in the loop as much as I feel I can, and in the meantime if Arsenal could make my day to day life as stress free as possible, I’d really appreciate that.

Someone have a word with Mikel and the lads.

#1606. Nottingham Forest vs. Chelsea: How to watch, date, time, live stream and TV channel for Premier League clash

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 13:37

Nottingham Forest and Chelsea will attempt to earn a much-needed boost in the Premier League when they square off on Friday night.

Despite seven points separating these teams in the Premier League table, the home side are arguably the favourites to prevail from this fixture.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Premier League match will kick off at 8pm, UK time, on Saturday.

This Premier League game between Nottingham Forest and Chelsea will be held at the City Ground, the home stadium of Forest.

Last season's corresponding fixture ended in a 3-0 victory for Chelsea, albeit in a game where Forest - then with Ange Postecoglou at the helm - squandered a number of opportunities.

The Premier League contest will be available on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League for viewers in the UK.

Sky customers can access the Premier League match on Sky Go and on the Sky Sports app, while it is also available via Now TV's Sports membership.

Sky Sports will show highlights, including any goals which have been scored, on their social media and YouTube channels, as well as on their dedicated app.

Meanwhile, those wishing to watch highlights on Match of the Day will have to wait until Saturday evening, with the programme starting at 10.30pm.

Both teams head into this fixture with question marks over their physicality, an issue which Oliver Glasner addressed in his pre-match press conference.

Forest begin the latest batch of games sitting in 17th position in the Premier League table, but they can move into 14th place with victory on Friday night.

Eight teams - including Chelsea - possess a worse defensive record than Forest, emphasising the feeling that they could quickly move up the standings if they resolve their issues in the final third.

On the back of three defeats in four matches and with 20 goals conceded in 11 games, Chelsea will be perceived to be ideal opponents for Forest.

While Chelsea have the opportunity to move into fifth place, they are highly likely to end the weekend in the bottom half of the table should they lose in the East Midlands.

#1603. It’ll be Ben White on the night

Arsenal lads were in action, and on the scoresheet, last night as England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid. Ezri Konsa made it 2-0 with a close range header, Spain might wonder who was marking him (I think it was supposed to be Marc Cucurella) but the movement was really sharp. Then a couple of minute later, Ben White fired England into a 3-0 lead, with Cucurella also in close attendance.

Obviously I’m not especially invested in the national sides of other countries, but I was pleased for Ben White after all the nonsense he’s been through with England. The worst sections of the media have fanned the flames against him, and it doesn’t take much to rile up those who are already of a jingoistic persuasion. As we’ve seen since seen with stories about Steve Holland being hugely unpopular at Man Utd, there’s a common denominator, and it’s not Ben White.

Holland was the one who sparked the issue originally when he was working with Gareth Southgate, so hopefully another goal for the Arsenal defender (he got one a few months back I think), and being part of a famous win in Spain will win around some of those fans who were giving him stick. I also feel quite confident that even if there is a cohort who won’t forgive Ben White for the crime of Steve Holland being a dickhead, he probably won’t care too much. Look at the reactions of his teammates and manager to the goal, and that’s tells you plenty.

He was also involved in a minor scuffle going off at half-time, which also seemed to involved Konsa and Martin Zubimendi, but I’m sure it was just heat of the moment stuff. Although Spain got two back after England went down to 10 men, they made the fatal mistake of starting Mikel Merino. How was he supposed to come off the bench and get a vital goal then? Silly Luis de la Fuenta, bloke’s a fraud.

Elsewhere over the weekend, Viktor Gyokeres scored twice for Sweden, both from the penalty spot. We just need more penalties. This is the key to unlocking him. Riccardo Calafiori played the full 90 as Italy went down 4-1 to Belgium (ouch), Martin Odegaard played 90 as Norway beat Wales, and there are some more games to come this week with Germany facing Netherlands tonight (Kai v Timber), the Brazilians are in action in Singapore, and apparently Christos Tzolis is fit to play for Greece after having an MRI.

Maybe it’s my own recent experiences, but I don’t care for the idea he needs an MRI. I get it, it’s probably for his knee or hamstring or something, but it feels like if you need one of those to know if you’re fit, you’re probably not feeling 100% anyway. I guess this will be one Mikel Arteta will keep a close eye on tonight when Greece host Serbia and Tzolis inevitably starts. Ideally, these will be useful minutes for him, and help him deliver for us but you can’t help but worry considering he picked up an injury in the last Interlull.

Finally for today, it looks as if a Declan Rice contract extension is close. Speaking while on England duty, he said:

“A new contract is hopefully on the horizon soon. I’m extremely lucky to be at a club like Arsenal where the manager shows me so much trust and teammates who put so much energy and effort into to me.

“I’m extremely lucky not to have to worry about that stuff, and it makes playing football far more easier.”

This is, by any measure, a no-brainer. I don’t think there’s a club in the world that would turn him down if he were available, and his importance to Arsenal is just obvious. In a world when £100m+ transfers often struggle to provide value, this is one of the exceptions. If you went back to 2023 and had to do it all again, even if you added another £20m or £30m to the fee we paid West Ham, it would be worth it. It’s likely to be the kind of deal that sees him play out the rest of his prime years in red and white, and let’s hope there are more trophies along the way to accompany that.

Right, I have to leave it there for this morning. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

The pod should be out around around midday. Until then, have a good one – after which I’m gonna be off for a couple of days but the lads will keep things ticking here until I get back.

#1602. Frosinone vs Parma - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 13:47

Both beaten 5-1 last weekend, Frosinone and Parma will aim to bounce back when they clash at Stadio Benito Stirpe on Saturday.

Despite suffering consecutive defeats for the first time this term, the hosts are still 12 points above their visitors in the Serie A standings.

Frosinone made an unexpectedly strong start to their latest comeback campaign, scoring freely while winning six of their first 11 fixtures after returning to Serie A.

However, Massimiliano Alvini's attack-minded side then suffered a rare setback, going down 1-0 to Cagliari, before they were well beaten just after the international break.

Two goals down within 20 minutes, the Canarini continued to fly forward, but they never really recovered and ultimately lost 5-1 to AC Milan at San Siro.

In fact, Frosinone have only claimed two points on the road since beating Fiorentina at the end of August, so their form at Stadio Stirpe has kept them tucked inside the top half.

After narrowly losing their first home fixture against Juventus, they have since won all of the next five, so confidence should still be high when lowly Parma come to town.

While their promoted hosts sit seventh in Serie A, Parma are hovering above the relegation zone with just eight points on the board.

Like Frosinone, they were thumped 5-1 last week, as Roma stormed to victory at Stadio Tardini, with Capocannoniere leader Donyell Malen helping himself to four goals.

That was the Gialloblu's eighth defeat from their first 12 league games, and the recent hiring of their second-highest Serie A scorer has hardly had an impact.

Alberto Gilardino has only celebrated one win since succeeding Carlos Cuesta, who kept the Emilian club afloat last term, but that lone success did come on the road.

Following a run of six straight away defeats, Parma recently beat Atalanta 3-0 in Bergamo, so they will aim to claim more points when they head south on Saturday.

Now trailing Malen in the race to be crowned Italy's top scorer, Frosinone striker Antonio Raimondo is still sidelined by injury - and his deputy is also unavailable.

Daniel Birligea bagged a brace against Lecce before scoring for Romania in their recent Nations League camp, but he strained a hamstring in Milan and has been ruled out for the next few weeks.

So, it remains to be seen whether Alvini selects support forwards Fares Ghedjemis, Romano Schmid and Giorgi Kvernadze - each of whom have provided four Serie A assists - or Slovak centre-forward Tomas Bobcek to lead the hosts' attack.

On the absence front, Florian Grillitsch has yet to recover from a thigh problem, but left-back Gabriele Bracaglia can return after serving a one-match ban.

While Parma will welcome back Abdoulaye Ndiaye from suspension, Argentine striker David Romero is still ruled out by a serious shoulder injury; defensive duo Diego Carlos (thigh) and Dominik Drobnic (foot) are also doubts.

In Romero's absence, Simone Lontani could partner El Bilal Toure, but Nesta Elphege is also a contender after scoring the Gialloblu's lone goal against Roma.

Palmisani; Oyono, Monterisi, Calvani, Bracaglia; Masini, Calo; Ghedjemis, Schmid, Kvernadze; Bobcek

Daffara; Delprato, Troilo, Ndiaye; Britschgi, Fabbian, Sierro, Keita, Valeri; Elphege, Toure

Frosinone can arrest their decline with another home win, as Parma are in grim form and could face a long fight to avoid the drop.

Notably, the Canarini tend to start fast - scoring a league-high 11 goals inside the first 30 minutes - while their visitors have yet to score before the half-hour mark.

#1600. Divine Dowman does it again

It’s Andrew A covering for Andrew M, who’s playing hooky again. I suppose after 24 years of writing this blog, a few bad habits are bound to creep in…

I’m not going to lie, it’s been a difficult week. Fortunately, a lifetime of watching Arsenal has given me plenty of practice at making bad jokes when I don’t know what else to say.

It’s either that or tears, and my eye juice reserves are running low after reading just a fraction of the thousands of messages you sent over the weekend. Bluesky, Reddit, X, Discord, Facebook, Patreon. Wherever I looked, there you were, sending love to Blogs. It was beautiful to see.

And to the handful of you who got in touch with me or people I know because you thought Friday’s update was about my health, please hold that thought. I’m fine. Touch wood. There are, in fact, two Andrews at Arseblog, and I’m the other one.

Having been crowned the “World’s Youngest Boy” by James on yesterday’s Arsecast Extra, Max Dowman set yet another record last night, becoming England under-21s’ youngest scorer with the winner in a 3-2 victory over France in filthy conditions in Bristol.

I’d planned to watch from kick-off, but gave up when I realised the game wasn’t on any of the 5,000 channels I pay £150 a month for. Then I saw on social media that Ethan Nwaneri, playing as a number 10, had laid on a couple of goals. So I did the clever thing and googled it. Turns out I needed the official England app and an account. Eyes still rolling, I tried to set up a login, only to find out I already had one. Cue the password reset process, verification codes and me losing the will to live. Just let me watch some fucking children play football in the rain!

By the time I got the stream, it was nearly half-time. At least that gave me a chance to catch up on Nwaneri’s two assists, both of which were Ozil-esque. First he drove down the left and slipped a neat ball inside for Mikey Moore, currently on loan at Cologne, to finish. Then came a teasing dink to the back post that Southampton’s Divin Mubama met first time. Given how little Nwaneri has played for Dortmund lately, it was a welcome reminder of what he can do.

It feels a bit silly to say Max, who was named player of the match, looked comfortable at this level when he’s already got a Premier League winners’ medal next to his GCSE textbooks, but he really did.

Watching him is like reading someone’s really nice handwriting. Even the everyday stuff looks lovely. A touch to bring the ball under control, a little turn, and suddenly the defender who was right up his arse is looking at the back of his shirt. I’ll never get tired of watching him do that.

As both sides made changes, I expected Lee Carsley to take him off. Instead, he played the full 90 and dug Arsenal teammate Tommy Setford out of a hole. The goalkeeper was at fault for the only goal in Friday’s defeat to Portugal and had another difficult night, spilling a cross into his own net. The rain hardly helped, and the 20-year-old has been doing well on loan at Stevenage, but it was a horrible one to concede.

When Brest’s Giovani Versini whipped in an equaliser with five minutes left, it looked like England would have to settle for a draw, but Dowman’s tap-in settled it with a minute to spare. Who knows, Dowman and Nwaneri could be on the same pitch again next week when Dortmund visit the Emirates.

Elsewhere, Group 2 of League A of the UEFA Nations League (catchy naming scheme, lads) served up another bonkers evening. Jurrien Timber scored twice in the Netherlands’ 7-0 win over Christos Tzolis’ Greece on Friday, only for the Dutch to lose 5-0 to Kai Havertz’s Germany in Berlin. There were some lovely goals from the Germans – including two from Florian Wirtz – who are finding their feet under Jurgen Klopp. Timber and Havertz both came off midway through the second half, seemingly unscathed. Timber’s pride aside, anyway.

Tzolis, meanwhile, was cleared to play after an MRI scan and got through 88 minutes of Greece’s 1-0 win over Serbia. All three sides finished on 11 points, with Germany and the Netherlands going through on goal difference at Greece’s expense.

Tonight, Martin Odegaard’s Norway face Denmark, while Viktor Gyokeres will look to extend his record-breaking scoring run for Sweden away at Poland. Piero Hincapie’s Ecuador take on Bolivia, Big Gabi and Bruno are in Singapore with Brazil, and Cristhian Mosquera and Marli Salmon are in action for Spain under-21s and England under-19s, respectively.

Closer to home, The Athletic ran two Arsenal contract stories in quick succession. James reports that Timber has agreed a new long-term deal, while David Ornstein says Declan Rice’s extension will take him through to 2031. Arsenal already had the option to keep Rice until 2029, so the new deal effectively buys them two more years and gives him a sizeable pay rise for the next four and a half. If he keeps playing as he has been, I can’t imagine many Arsenal fans quibbling with that.

For what it’s worth, we’ve heard on the grapevine that David Raya’s new contract is all but done, too, which means the club are making good progress with the lads whose deals expire in 2028, a list that also includes Odegaard, Havertz, Mikel Merino and our two backup keepers.

There was an interesting discussion on Arsenal Vision’s ‘Friday Night Clive’ podcast about Arsenal elongating their “winning window” while having one eye on the next iteration of the team. If you hand expensive new contracts to players hurtling towards their thirties, you leave yourself financially exposed and potentially blocking pathways for up-and-coming talent. No doubt the club and manager are keenly aware of that. I just wonder how much you can expect the latter to focus on the faraway future when the dynasty he craves has to start in the here and now.

If this week has taught me anything, it’s that there’s something to be said for seizing the day. Admittedly, that’s easier when it’s Arsenal’s money I’m volunteering to spend.

If you’re about to part with some of your own (smooth segue, Allen) this year’s Arseblog Christmas Gift Guide is up.

I spent some of last week rounding up Arsenal bits and pieces I’d be happy to find under the tree. Mostly, I wanted to point you towards the independent makers, artists and writers producing stuff I like. In many cases, what I’ve picked is just a small sample of what they do, so have a nose around.

If you’ve got a recommendation of your own, pop the link in the form at the bottom and I’ll take a look.

Right, I’d better crack on with the day job. Lewis is on duty tomorrow and, all being well, Andrew M should be back here before the week is out.

#1599. GdS: Bright foundations for the future – Milan, Inter and Juventus’ financial years compared

Last night, a report was published comparing the financials of AC Milan, Juventus and Inter and the findings are very interesting.

The big three bring a lot of attention to Italy and their footballing ecosystem, but that’s not all. Indeed, all three bring in vast amounts of money and have done so for years, which has helped them establish this dominance. However, their records last season show that a change could be on the way.

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, via Calciomercato.com, Inter recorded the highest revenue last season of €518 million, Juventus slotted in with €474.4m and then the Rossoneri finished ‘last’ with a revenue of €464.6m.

However, the profits – about that – of all three clubs didn’t line up in the same order. Inter recorded a €23m loss, then it was Milan with a €24m loss – largely helped by the summer signings – and Juventus finished last with a €66m loss.

Considering the Nerazzurri’s sporting successes in recent years, it makes sense why revenues are considerably higher, especially when looking at their Champions League records. For example, not being in Europe cost the Diavolo €54m between 2024/25 and 2025/26.

In terms of squad cost, the Biaconeri were uncontested at the top, with a wage of €210m per season. Inter finished just below with €204m per season, whilst the Rossoneri ‘only’ spent €146m. Of course, this is still lucrative.

All in all, the foundations laid at Casa Milan are looking strong and if they can become more successful, their revenues could rocket up.

#1598. New deals for all, Odegaard’s brilliance, assists galore

Good morning! I’ve got to say, if I worked at Arsenal and I wasn’t getting a new contract this international break, I think I’d be taking it pretty personally.

After Monday’s news that both Jurrien Timber and Declan Rice have agreed new deals with the club, Tuesday brought the news that fellow 2023 signing David Raya was next in line, swiftly followed by reports that Riccardo Calafiori will also be handed a new deal, and Piero Hincapie will be getting improved terms, too.

Since the end of the 2024-25 season, there have already been new deals for Gabriel, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ethan Nwaneri, William Saliba, Bukayo Saka, and, of course, Mikel Arteta. With the latest raft of agreements on top of those, that’s a lot of important people tied down for the next few years.

These deals will mean everyone other than Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard, Ben White, Mikel Merino, and Kepa is contracted to the club until at least 2029. That’s a nice feeling, isn’t it? There will be some decisions to be made over a couple of those players and whether it’s time to refresh, you’d imagine, but the bulk of the squad should be staying put and continuing to compete together – with a couple of additions supplementing them, of course – for the next couple of years at least.

Of those four (plus Kepa) mentioned above, you’d have to think Odegaard is the next priority when it comes to renewals, given his importance on and off the pitch and his current form.

I was in a bar here in Berlin catching up with a fellow Arsenal fan yesterday evening (hello, if you’re reading!) and they had Norway’s game in Denmark on. It’s fair to say the skipper continued his fine start to the season.

After Norway went two down against the run of play, Odegaard sprung into action. No player had as many touches on the night, and he was involved in all three Norway goals.

He stole the ball for the goal that made it 2-1, which, by the way, we should have a word for. We have the word equaliser for when it goes to 2-2, but we don’t have a word for the goal that shortens the lead. The Germans call it an Anschlusstor – literally a ‘connecting goal’, the goal that means the scores are now just one apart.

Anyway, Odegaard, pressing as he always does, stole the ball from goalkeeper Mads Hermansen, then selflessly left the tap-in for Erling Haaland. He then scored the equaliser, a goal reminiscent of his opening day strike against Coventry if we’re honest: he didn’t hit it well, he got a bit lucky. But: right place, right time and all that.

And, finally, it was Odegaard’s ferociously whipped in free-kick that struck the hand of Joachim Andersen and allowed Haaland to convert from the penalty spot late into added time. If you’ve got a few minutes, you can see the highlights of his performance here – some of the touches are more than worth your time.

A good night’s work, especially after he was suffering with a stomach bug last week.

It wasn’t just the captain in action yesterday, either. Piero Hincapie played just over an hour for Ecuador overnight, there were assists for Gabriel and Bruno Guimaraes as Brazil beat Singapore 7-0 earlier on in the day, and then an assist for Viktor Gyokeres too as Sweden drew with Poland.

That looks like something he’s clearly worked on – getting his body in the way of the defender and, rather than holding the ball up, looking to direct it towards an oncoming runner. His assist for Declan Rice in Munich obviously looked pretty similar, and it’s not something we saw too much of last season.

In fact, I thought I’d have a quick look, and Gyokeres has 13 key passes (a pass that leads a shot from a team-mate) in the Premier League and Champions League this season. He’s delivering a key pass every 28.4 minutes. Last season he had a key pass every 104 minutes across those two competitions. It’s hard not to conclude that he’s been working on that side of his game, and these Giroud-esque back-to-goal touches for team-mates are more than welcome.

So, plenty of assists this break. Now we just need to harness that at Newcastle on Saturday and actually have someone to stick the ball in the back of the net at the end of those moves. Thankfully – knock on wood – it seems the players have made it through the break unscathed (there was also another behind-closed-doors appearance for William Saliba – a nod to Tom Canton for that story) and should be raring to go.

Lastly, I want to point you towards Arseblog News, where Andrew A wrote something last night on the death of double-winner Peter Storey, one of just eight players to make over 500 appearances for the club. That first double is such an enormous part of our history wouldn’t have happened without Storey’s nerves of steel in the FA Cup semi-final.

#1597. Birmingham City vs Bolton Wanderers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 13:52

Aiming to remain unbeaten at home in the league this season, promotion-hunting Birmingham City host struggling Bolton Wanderers at St Andrew's @ Knighthead Park in the Championship on Saturday afternoon.

Blues were the latest side to take advantage of Burnley's Turf Moor misery on Wednesday night, whilst the Wanderers suffered defeat on their own patch by West Bromwich Albion.

As has been the case after each of their three Championship defeats so far this season, Birmingham City bounced back from last weekend's Stoke City disappointment by claiming three points, this time at the expense of crisis-hit Burnley.

Chris Davies's side have already equalled the number of away victories that they managed across the entirety of last season (6) courtesy of August Priske's seventh league goal of the term and an own goal from Clarets winger Jaydon Banel at Turf Moor.

Following seven wins from their past nine second-tier contests, Birmingham are occupying fourth position in the Championship table, three points behind current pacesetters Middlesbrough and Stoke.

Apart from a 6-1 battering by Brentford in the EFL Cup, Blues have been impressive at St Andrew's this season, with Saturday's hosts unbeaten across their opening eight home league battles (W4 D4).

In fact, Birmingham last experienced Second City defeat in the Championship at the beginning of April, and Davies has lost just three home league games since taking charge during the summer of 2024.

Sliding towards the relegation zone, Bolton Wanderers have now won just one of their past seven Championship contests (D2 L4) after losing to West Brom at the Toughsheet Community Stadium earlier in the week.

A second-half penalty from Ruben Rodrigues levelled the scores momentarily following Albion's opener, however, further strikes from Norwegian duo Aune Heggebo and Felix Horn Myhre sentenced the Wanderers to a fourth defeat in their past six games.

Winless in their past five games (D1 L4) at the Toughsheet, Bolton's last three victories have all arrived on the road, with Saturday's underdog visitors beating Norwich City (4-3), Wolverhampton Wanderers (3-1) and Charlton Athletic (1-0) since late September.

There is no doubting that the newly-promoted side are one of the favourites to suffer relegation this season, with Steven Schumacher's troops currently six points clear of the bottom three.

Bolton were defeated on their most recent trip to St Andrew's in October 2024 but were one of only three teams to beat Birmingham during their record-breaking League One title romp of 2024-25.

Birmingham defender Ethan Laird missed the Burnley win after picking up a knock at Stoke last weekend, with the right-back a doubt for the Second City match on Saturday.

As a result, Bright Osayi-Samuel is likely to retain his spot in defence, with Dael Fry set to drop out in order to make room for the available-again Christoph Klarer.

Liam Millar, Jhon Solis and Jay Stansfield were rested for the final 15 minutes at Turf Moor, with the trio all set to start once again this weekend.

There is likely to be alteration on the right flank, though, where Patrick Roberts could be the key to unlocking a deep Bolton block.

Bolton rotated leading marksman Sam Dalby out of the starting side on Wednesday but the Englishman is fully expected to return to the XI on Saturday.

Ben Davies could feature against his former loan employers, whilst Samuel Illing-Junior is in line for another start following a bright display against West Brom.

Birmingham City possible starting lineup:

Beadle; Osayi-Samuel, Neumann, Klarer, Cochrane; Iwata, Solis; Roberts, Stansfield, Millar; Priske

Bolton Wanderers possible starting lineup:

Bazunu; Stephenson, Brunt, Forino-Joseph, Conway; Simons, Sheehan; Larrazabal, Ito, Illing-Junior; Dalby

After winning four straight home matches by an aggregate scoreline of 12-1, Birmingham are the overwhelming favourites for another Second City success this weekend.

Bolton have recent experience of producing a shock result in the West Midlands, however, we feel that Davies's St Andrew's juggernaut will be too strong in this matchup.

#1596. Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn

At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x

As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a new contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

“A joy to have him,” said Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

“Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta says Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z

Dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” said Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”

Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

It was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.

Arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

Given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

The only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub

On managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta said: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady says Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf

Asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta said: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”

He added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta said: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

“Individually some big performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”

Among Arsenal’s substitutes, Julienne took 24 in 26 minutes while Odegaard had 25 in 14 minutes.

Ipswich Town 2 Arsenal 4 (Akpom) Davis picks out Akpom who swivels to deceive Konsa before sweeping home. There was perhaps a foul in the build-up as Lewis-Skelly appeared to get held back by the goalscorer as he scrambled to get back.

Dowman seemingly makes history with every touch of the ball. A remarkable talent.

Arsenal are finishing this match with a 16-year-old, 17-year-old and two 18-year-olds on the pitch. A good evening for the academy.

And right on cue, Salmon picks up the ball on the halfway line and drives forward, eventually forcing a foul from Nunez who goes into the book for his troubles.

Gyokeres finally gets a sniff at goal but Greaves is wise to his movement in behind and times a slide-tackle perfectly to poke the ball off for a corner.

Ibrahim comes on for Zubimendi before it is taken and joins the crew congregated at the far post but Walton punches Odegaard’s delivery away.

A really assured performance from Salmon, who has completed all 61 one of his passes and marshalled Flemming and Akpom with maturity beyond his years.

Chance! A high regain puts Mehmeti into a promising position in the right half-space, but his cross in to Akpom comes to nothing.

Tzolis, who is booed by the home fans owing to his Norwich connections, has a glimpse at goal but is immediately closed down before Ipswich earn a corner after a swift transition but it is easily dealt with.

There is an appeal for a handball off an Arsenal defender in the second phase of the set-piece but Egeli is offside so it matters not.

Just the 13 touches for Gyokeres tonight, make of that what you will...

Arteta shuffles the pack again, taking off Eze and Madueke for Tzolis and Odegaard.

Florentino tries his luck from the edge of the box, but his effort is comfortably saved by Kepa despite taking a slight deflection off Konsa’s Achilles.

It has been a relatively quiet night for Eze as Arsenal have prioritised attacks down the right. He twists this way and that and escapes the clutches of Furlong but his eventual effort sails well over.

Davis gets his teeth into the action right away. He swings in a cross from the left but it’s smothered by Kepa.

Ipswich’s substitutes have breathed some life into their attack. Akpom fires a cross-cum-shot towards goal but strikes the side-netting.

Another couple of substitutions for O’Neil, who will now be thinking about Everton next weekend. Davis and Walle Egeli are on for Ouattara and McAteer.

For those who are into your statistics, another Dowman goal here would create some history...

The record for the youngest hat-trick scorer across all professional tiers of English football belongs to Trevor Francis.

Playing for Birmingham City against Bolton Wanderers in Division Two on February 20, 1971, Francis scored four goals in a 4-0 win at just 16 years and 307 days old.

Guimaraes makes way for 18-year-old Julienne.

Ipswich Town 1 Arsenal 4 (Mehmeti) Clarke makes an immediate impact, bursting down the left before cutting the ball back to Mehmeti who had just held his run and is able to beat Kepa from 10 yards out.

Ipswich have been outgunned in the centre of the park, with Arsenal seemingly always creating plus-one and even plus-two situations.

O’Neil makes a pair of changes, replacing Philogene and Flemming with Clarke and former Arsenal striker Akpom.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 4 (Merino) Arsenal work the ball infield from the right in instalments, Madueke feeding Zubimendi who passes through Dowman to Merino on the edge of the box who opens up his body before guiding the ball around Walton.

Arsenal are FLYING!Merino puts another goal away for the Gunners 🔥 pic.twitter.com/nrzHHk1bou

Max Dowman was first spotted by Arsenal at four years old. He’s been running past opponents and scoring goals ever since. Now he’s just doing it on the professional stage, in front of the watching world, but it still looks completely normal to him.

Chance! It could, and maybe should, have been four. Merino threads a wonderful through-ball beyond Ipswich’s final line of defence and Madueke steals in to poke the ball across the face of goal with the outside of his left boot. Gyokeres was in the middle but could not divert the ball goalwards.

Kepa stretches to claim a looped Flemming cross which had echoes of the Spaniard’s game-defining error in last year’s League Cup final. This time he collects with a minimum of fuss. That Flemming was so far out on the left will be of concern to O’Neil.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 3 (Dowman) Madueke picks out Zubimendi in the box who in turn finds Dowman in the right half space and he gallops on to the ball before arrowing the ball past Walton. The assist had grazed Greaves’ outstretched arm and would surely have led to a penalty had Dowman not done the honours.

Max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x

Arsenal’s kick-off routines caused a stir last season, but this term they have mixed things up once more. Here, Zubimendi lays off Lewis-Skelly, who punches in a line-breaking pass to get Arsenal on the front foot from the off.

Zubimendi gets us going again for the second 45 minutes. Konsa has replaced Gabriel at the interval.

Such is the midfielder’s versatility, his heat map tonight paints a wildly different picture to that from his 45 minutes at the Stadium of Light over the weekend. He has played the midfield-sentry role in Suffolk and has executed it well.

It is further evidence as to why Arteta was hell bent on signing him in the summer. You would imagine his all-conquering presence will relieve pressure from Rice and Zubimendi’s shoulders. They were out on their feet by the end of the last campaign.

Arteta’s nine changes are looking fairly sensible now. He will be particularly pleased to have seen fringe players like Dowman and Madueke get on the scoresheet so emphatically. Arsenal will need their full squad to achieve their lofty goals this season and that half will give Arteta confidence that they have enough firepower to last the course.

We’ll play one minute of time added on...

Arsenal inject a bit of calm to proceedings with a healthy spell of possession. Their horizontal and vertical rotations (Lewis-Skelly is now minding to drop into that Rice role alongside the centre-backs) are proving tricky for Ipswich to track.

Gyokeres gets a shot away after a clever run in behind by Merino but cannot get enough pace behind his strike to trouble Walton.

Mehmeti brings down a searching ball from deep and faces up to Gabriel as he enters Arsenal box. Such is the Brazilian’s poise, though, that even when the Ipswich forward appears to have worked a yard of space, he telescopes in his leg and stops Mehmeti’s advances with perfunctory ease.

Ipswich are getting more bodies forward, with both full-backs bombing on. The ball is worked out to Furlong out on the right but, in a promising position, he loses his footing and the ball rolls out of play.

Next comes a foray down the left, Philogene beats Salmon on the outside but Kepa gets down smartly to cut out his cross. The next goal will naturally go a long way to determining how this tie plays out.

Ipswich are in the ascendancy and Greaves heads goalwards off a corner but does not get the requisite contact to beat Kepa. Arsenal launch a swift counter which is snuffed out by McAteer, illegally, and he goes into the book.

Ipswich might have thrown the towel in at 2-0 but they are pushing quite hard here and have caused Arsenal a few problems since the second goal. Philogene looks particularly dangerous on the left flank.

Outtara has been Ipswich’s best attacking outlet and he threads another lovely ball into the path of Philogene who is just beaten to it by Gabriel. The subsequent corner is punched away by Kepa.

Kepa goes long and Greaves misjudges the flight of the ball. Madueke looks to be in, but Ipswich’s centre-half recovers well and is able to block the eventual effort.

Merino picks out Dowman between the lines and the teenager is straight into Ipswich’s backline. His effort is well-struck but is charged down and cleared to safety.

Better from Ipswich! Their best shot at getting back into this contest is through counters when Arsenal are not set, and here Outtara bursts down the left before swinging in a deep cross to Flemming who cuts the ball back to Mehmeti who fires the ball just over the crossbar.

Guimaraes is slotting in between Arsenal’s split centre-backs in Arsenal’s build-up and Ipswich are not prepared to go three vs three that high up the pitch meaning the Brazilian has all the time in the world to dictate play from there. We’ve seen this all season long from Rice.

Arsenal are in complete control. Madueke flashes a delivery across the face of goal which is just cut out by Kipre before Gyokeres can get a foot in.

Arsenal’s midfield is so powerful and they showed it there, as Guimaraes slammed into one tackle and then Merino followed up with another to create the chance for Madueke. Arsenal are completely dominant here.

A flurry of chances for Ipswich. Philogene’s lopping cross is tipped away by Kepa but the ball falls to Flemming at the back post and his effort pinballs around a thicket of Arsenal limbs before reaching Florentino on the edge of the box, whose effort sails over the bar.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 2 (Madueke) That is goal of Ipswich’s own making. Walton’s loose pass out is picked off by livewire Guimaraes, and Merino spins in a ball in behind for Madueke to stride on to and spear beyond Walton into the bottom corner.

Arsenal are flying 🔥Noni Madueke adds a second for the Gunners 🔴 pic.twitter.com/gAVmAI3odx

Florentino’s loose pass is picked off by Dowman and the youngster earns a free-kick as the Ipswich midfielder attempts to recover. It’s taken quickly and Eze bursts into the box - there is a half-hearted shout for a penalty as the ball appears to strike Ouattara’s arm but the contact appears incidental and the referee waves play on.

Max Dowman’s second goal for Arsenal is quite similar to his first, scored so thrillingly against Everton last season. On both occasions he has put an opposition defender face-first in the turf before scoring the goal. Outrageous ability with the ball at his feet.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn

Ipswich earn a free-kick on the left by-line but Gyokeres does his job at the near post and heads away Nunez’s delivery.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 1 (Dowman) Simply majestic. A simple one-two with Eze on the left has Dowman running at Ipswich’s defence. He drops his shoulder and sells Kipre a dream before stroking the ball beyond Walton. “1-0 to the champions” sing the travelling fans.

Lewis-Skelly bursts down the left and picks out Dowman on the edge of the box. He attempts to tee up Guimaraes but Nunez gets a toe in and is able to avert the danger.

Early indications suggest Zubimendi will play in the nominal right-back position, inverting into midfield when Arsenal build up.

Madueke picks up the ball on the right flank and drifts inside before Guimaraes’ effort from the edge of the box is blocked.

Flemming gets us started. Ipswich kicking from right to left.

The players emerge from the Portman Road tunnel, Ipswich in their customary home blue shirts and white shorts, Arsenal in red and also white shorts. Last week Arsenal were made to change into red shorts to avoid a similar clash with Napoli, but apparently that’s no problem tonight. Modern football for ya!
