#1534. Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

“I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was important for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Big cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

As we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

He has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré

"It's part of the decision that I took when I decided to join this club"Enzo Maresca responds to the doubts surrounding him filling Pep Guardiola's shoes 👇 pic.twitter.com/o6eUjQUOnU

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a new five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

His older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Checking in 🚌🚶‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/xWYGyaH7TY

Ⓒ Darling with the armband🧤 Grimshaw in goal⚡️ Ante on the rightYour Yellows for this evening ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/znOGtvyJyk

Your City side to take on Norwich 👊XI | Rulli, Lewis, Khusanov, Reis, O'Reilly, Bouaddi, Kovačić (C), Samba, Allan, Aït-Nouri, CherkiSUBS | Donnarumma, Anderson, Guéhi, Ndiaye, Fernández, Nunes, Semenyo, McAidoo, Braithwaite🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/LCA4WfACBf

Good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

These two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

#1533. Report: Liverpool to race Manchester United to forgotten defender

#1532. Man United predicted lineup vs. Brentford: Cunha, Shaw, Dalot decisions for Pochettino

By Oliver Thomas | 26 Nov 2026 16:05, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 17:09

Manchester United will be without at least three players for Saturday’s Premier League clash with Brentford at Old Trafford.

Carlos Baleba (hamstring), Benjamin Sesko (calf) and Manuel Ugarte (knee) all remain sidelined with injuries, while Marcus Rashford (hip), Luke Shaw (fitness) and Karl Darlow (knee) will all be assessed ahead of kickoff.

Shaw watched on as an unused substitute on Wednesday as Man United drew 2-2 with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League, and the left-back may be ready to start his first game since October 10.

If not, then Lisandro Martinez could be tasked with a start on the left side of a back four where he began against Sporting, while Diogo Dalot will hope to force his way back into the first XI at right-back ahead of Noussair Mazraoui.

Leny Yoro has seen his red card overturned following his eighth-minute dismissal in United’s 4-0 Premier League defeat at Liverpool last weekend. The Frenchman is likely to start alongside Harry Maguire at centre-back, with Matthijs de Ligt to continue as a substitute.

Youri Tielemans was sent off for two bookable offences against Sporting, but he is available to start in midfield on Saturday alongside Kobbie Mainoo, while Bruno Fernandes will continue in the number 10 role seeking to build on his brace netted in midweek.

Matheus Cunha served a continental ban against Sporting and is now free to return to Mauricio Pochettino’s side against Brentford, with either Amad Diallo or Joshua Zirkzee set to drop out as a result.

If Amad reverts to the bench, former Brentford attacker Bryan Mbeumo could move over to the right flank, but if Zirkzee makes way, Mbeumo will presumably lead the line as Cunha operates on the left flank.

Manchester United possible starting lineup:

Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, Maguire, Martinez; Mainoo, Tielemans; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Cunha; Zirkzee

#1531. Gary Neville tears into Man United's Matthijs de Ligt for 'unforgivable' defending that led to Leny Yoro's red card - and claims duo played like 'they have never had basic defensive training'

Published: 12:23 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026

Gary Neville led the criticism of Manchester United's defending in the opening minutes against Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino's reign started in disastrous fashion at Anfield.

After just eight minutes, his plans were thrown into tatters when errors from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro saw the latter sent off before Liverpool took a swift lead.

A long ball from Ronald Araujo should have been dealt with easily by De Ligt, but the Dutchman found himself in no man's land, left the ball, and Alexander Isak raced clear.

That left Yoro scrambling to try to recover the situation for his side, but Isak stepped across him and he ended up fouling the Reds forward.

Referee Sam Barrott wasted no time in pulling out the red card, and United found themselves reduced to 10 men just minutes into a vital clash.

And former United defender Neville didn't hold back when it came to his analysis as he tore into the two players at fault.

Leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 pic.twitter.com/VKYvckvBBP

Gary Neville torn into Manchester United duo Leny Yoro (right) and Matthijs de Ligt after the former was sent off

Neville (pictured) questioned why the duo were playing as if they had 'never had basic training of how to play in defence'

'When I saw De Ligt's name on the team sheet I have to admit I was absolutely stunned,' he said, speaking on Sky Sports. 'And the reason I was stunned was because of this. If you'd watched him in Como four weeks ago he was very much well off it and that is just a basic ball over the top.

'It's his problem to start with, Yoro can be further across, but De Ligt is miles away from it, then Yoro has to get further round, he reacts late, his anticipation is poor. It's so clumsy from Yoro, he makes a lot of these types of mistakes.

'You could argue Isak delays to make sure Yoro runs into him, but it's naivety.'

Pochettino was left scrambling to think of ideas to tighten up the defence but, before he could bring Harry Maguire on, it was 2-0 through Florian Wirtz.

Maguire eventually came on but it felt like too little, too late.

'We saw him in Como and he has been out for a year,' Neville continued on De Ligt. 'It is really tough to come back. To have him out there in a game like this, he has been exposed. Yoro's positioning is poor, he has to be across, you have to cover your mate. It is bad all around from United.

'Michael Carrick will be watching and say that's what I was having to deal with.'

And his criticism didn't stop there. After having the chance to re-watch the incident, Neville's criticism grew even stronger.

De Ligt (left) failed to deal with a long ball as Alexander Isak (right) raced away before the foul

Former United captain Roy Keane (pictured) added that he was 'amazed' by the errors made

'It's as bad defending from two centre backs defending a long ball as you will see,' the former defender, who likened a return from a year out to playing after six pints of alcohol, added. 'De Ligt is well out of it - he's been out so I have some sympathy. But between them, to let the ball beat you, it's unforgivable.

'It is shocking. Whilst Man United have those types of defenders in their team, they have no chance of keeping a clean sheet.

'It's basic understanding of how to play a position. It's the fundamentals. It's like these guys have never had basic training of how to play in defence.'

Former United captain Roy Keane chimed in too, adding at half-time: 'It doesn't matter if it's a back four or back five, you do the basics right.

'I'm amazed at this level, I know he's been out a while, but it's really poor defending. He's never getting that ball.

'If you're a defender you always expect the worst. Isak's done well and I actually don't think he's going to get the ball.

'There's no way he's (Yoro) getting the ball, it's clumsy by United. Straight ball over the top and he's in big trouble. But there's no way he's getting that ball. I know he's quick and sharp but it's really poor defending. Players not smelling danger.'

#1530. Amorim discusses everchanging Milan landscape, constant injuries and winning trophies: “Have to be ready”

Ahead of a do-or-die clash against Olympiacos for AC Milan in the Europa League, Ruben Amorim spoke to the media.

There’s still time for Milan to turn around their Europa League campaign, but so far, it’s been one to forget. Their successes in the league have often been reduced thanks to poor performances in midweek, and that cannot happen again.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

After a dismantling of Frosinone at the weekend, Amorim’s side should be full of confidence and wholesale rotations are not expected in Greece tomorrow night. So, logically, that confidence should continue and there should be several reasons to feel hopeful of a result.

However, as we know, there have been similar feelings heading into Europe this season and the Rossoneri have often not followed up with performances of similar levels. Tomorrow must be different.

Speaking alongside Ardon Jashari, the Portuguese discussed the challenge his team will face tomorrow, as MilanNews relays.

What do you ask of the team for tomorrow? More volume in attack? How do you plan to support Ramos?

“It’s not about helping Ramos, but also Camarda and everyone up front. It’s a fact that we need to improve in the final third. The only thing we can do is improve our principles. We need to improve on these little things, and that’s the only way I can help my players.

“Against Olympiacos, it will be a different match than the one against Frosinone, just as it will be different than the one against Cagliari.

“We need to improve, even in our defending. We’ve almost always conceded a goal, so that’s another area we need to improve.”

How would you describe Olympiacos as a team?

“Thank you for the welcome. They’re a strong team. They’re aggressive, especially at home. I’ve played here twice, and it was tough for me. I know their coach and what he wants to do.

“They play compact, positive football, 4-3-3; they change a lot, they rotate, they have Jota, a lot of Portuguese players. They’re a strong team, and with their fans there, it’ll be a tough match.

“Chiquinho is a great talent, but very impulsive. I hope he plays well tomorrow, but I hope he still has a great career ahead of him.”

Does AC Milan’s growth also involve Europe?

“To be a good team, you have to do well both in the league and in Europe. That’s the only way to be a good team. We have to be, especially at Milan.

“My compliments? I’m always waiting for things to go badly, because it doesn’t take much to change the situation. That’s what I’m trying to make my players understand, because it won’t always be this way.

“We’re at the beginning of a process, and I think we need everyone. We lost Pavlovic, Modric, Saelemaekers, Chukwueze, and everyone has to be ready, because there are no excuses at big clubs. We have to be ready for this.

“I can’t believe we lost all these games in Europe because we rotated. We have to always be ready and approach the games like against Inter, Frosinone, and Genoa. We’re building so many things. Tomorrow is another test for us.

“I believe in all competitions, but if we can win them all, no. Scudetto? I haven’t changed my mind. This year is difficult, but if we have the chance to fight, we’ll do it. I won’t change for the compliments, because I’m waiting and so are you.

“You’re waiting [for criticism]. Tomorrow we have to win, because if we don’t… I’m ready for that.”

Is football becoming dangerous for the mental and physical health of players and coaches?

“It’s difficult to protect players considering the times we’re living in. Younger players will be more willing to live with criticism. It’s different from my reality. It’s difficult to control this.

“When you asked me about GTA, I’d rather my players play every day rather than scroll through social media. What I mean is that we want more time between games. I’m talking about the product, not my life.

“I’m talking about the quality of the football product. I don’t know what Fabregas meant, but it’s the evolution of society, of football, which is a business, and we have to be ready.

“Social media, and all that stuff, is very difficult for players, who in any case live with more criticism than I do. After Frosinone, I haven’t read anything, because that’s how I want to live my life.”

You have a lot of experience as a player: what do you expect from the stadium tomorrow?

“I know the atmosphere here. It’s incredible. It’s important for my players to have this experience, even though there’s no stadium more difficult to play in than San Siro. We have to be ready in these kinds of stadiums.

“We lost 5-1 once, but I’m very focused on what we have to do, how we’ll start the match, I’m focused on these things. The atmosphere should be normal for these players, who are used to big events. We have to be competitive and ready.”

#1529. Opinion: Julian Ward has found a perfect attacker for Liverpool

Liverpool have been constantly upgrading their team over the last couple of years.

The Anfield outfit have spent well over £600 million on new players to try and improve their ranks.

And, while some of the deal that they've struck have worked out, some still need to prove their worth.

Indeed, the performances of Liverpool's squad as a whole have improved thanks to the appointment of Andoni Iraola but, it's clear that there are still some problems that need rectifying.

Whether the Reds need to sign back-ups or replacements for their starting XI, change is needed so that they don't fall too far behind their title rivals.

So, the perfect attacker now being found by Liverpool is rather exciting.

Liverpool's attack has been one of their main focuses when improving their squad.

The Anfield outfit have spent well over £300 million on attackers alone over the last couple of years but, it still seems like the club aren't fully happy with the options that they have at their disposal.

That is obviously a crazy statement to share as, just this summer, £123 million was spent on Bradley Barcola alone.

But, with how many players Premier League clubs buy every season, there's no wonder why clubs have to constantly spend to keep up with their rivals.

And now, thanks to an update from X account Mekteb-i Gala, who have 50,000 followers, it seems like another attacker has made his way onto Liverpool's shortlist.

"EXCLUSIVE | PSG, Manchester City, Liverpool, Atletico Madrid, Como and Juventus are monitoring Yunus Akgün in every match," they wrote.

"They are in the process of gathering information on the player."

Yunus Akgun could be an unreal back-up option for Liverpool

Akgun is almost certainly a player that most Liverpool fans won't have heard of.

The Turkiye international is a 26-year-old winger who contributed to 21 goals across all competitions for Fenerbahce last term.

He's also had previous experience of English football as he spent the 2023-24 campaign on loan to Leicester in the Championship.

Unfortunately, his time in England didn't pan out as well as he would have hoped as he only contributed to six goals in the 29 games that he featured in.

Obviously, since most of his career has been spent in Turkiye, he probably wouldn't be able to get straight into Iraola's starting XI but, since he can play as a number 10 or a winger on either side, he could be an extremely useful back-up option for Liverpool to have.

These links are all just rumours at the moment but, of all the players who have been recently linked with Liverpool, Akgun feels like a really interesting deal for the Reds to explore, especially since they still need a back-up number 10 for Florian Wirtz.

#1528. Could Pep Guardiola succeed Thomas Tuchel as England manager after revealing his 'next step'?

By Naim Beneddra | 26 Nov 2026 16:12

Former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola has confirmed that he wants to move into international management when he returns to football, an admission that raises an intriguing question about England's long-term plans beyond Thomas Tuchel's tenure.

The Spaniard has been taking a break from management since leaving the Etihad Stadium at the end of the 2025-26 season, bringing an end to a remarkable decade in which he won six Premier League titles and the Champions League.

Although Guardiola has yet to establish a date for his return, the 55-year-old has a clear idea of what he wants to do next. His latest comments also shed light on how close he came to embarking on an international career last summer, when the Italian Football Federation approached him about taking charge of the Azzurri.

Speaking in an interview with his former Barcelona teammate Romario on Romario TV, Guardiola was asked whether there was a team he had never managed but would like to coach.

"A national team, which is my next step," replied the former Bayern Munich boss, who also explained that the timing of Italy's approach had prevented him from accepting the position.

"If it had happened a year or two earlier, I probably would have accepted," Guardiola admitted, explaining that his conversations with Paolo Maldini and Leonardo had taken place when he felt he needed a break from football.

Having spent 18 years in club management, Guardiola was reluctant to commit himself to another project so soon after leaving City. Italy subsequently appointed Roberto Mancini, while the Spaniard remains without a managerial position and has given no indication of when his sabbatical will end.

The United States are another potential destination following Mauricio Pochettino's departure to Manchester United. Guardiola has previously spoken enthusiastically about the potential of the American national team, although the prospect of managing England may also warrant consideration given the Football Association's reported interest in him in the past.

According to The Athletic, Guardiola was the FA's preferred candidate to replace Gareth Southgate following Euro 2024, with a verbal agreement reportedly in place before the Spaniard opted to remain at Manchester City.

His former Spain teammate Gaizka Mendieta has also identified England as a potential destination, alongside Brazil, believing that Guardiola would be attracted by the opportunity to compete for major international honours.

England's current managerial situation could prove compatible with Guardiola's desire to take an extended break. Tuchel signed a contract extension in February to lead the Three Lions through to Euro 2028 and reiterated his commitment to that agreement earlier this month.

The German, however, has also made no secret of his desire to return to club management once his England tenure comes to an end. Should he depart after the European Championship, his successor would have two years to prepare the national team for the 2030 World Cup.

By that stage, Guardiola would have spent two seasons away from the dugout. The prospect of working with players such as Jude Bellingham, Declan Rice, Cole Palmer and Phil Foden would certainly be interesting from a tactical perspective, particularly given his preference for technically accomplished midfielders capable of operating in several positions.

His familiarity with English football and previous experience of working with several England internationals would also ease certain aspects of the transition, although implementing his demanding tactical approach within the limited training windows available to national team managers would represent a new challenge.

There is currently nothing to suggest that the FA are looking beyond Tuchel or that Guardiola has identified England as his preferred destination. However, should the position become available in 2028, the circumstances could be considerably more favourable than when the FA reportedly approached him two years ago.

#1526. Opinion: Liverpool have found their perfect Alisson successor, but it's not who you think

Alisson is one of Liverpool's biggest-named players to be linked with an exit this summer.

The Brazilian's contract is set to expire in June 2027 and, right now, it doesn't feel like the Reds are going to offer him a new deal.

Indeed, rumours about both ends of the deal have been emerging and, even though the former Roma man has been an important asset for Liverpool this term, his age coupled with the sheer number of goalkeepers the Reds have on their books make a deal difficult.

Obviously, Alisson's time at the club has been well regarded. He's won two Premier League titles and one Champions League trophy.

But, since he's now in the twilight stages of his career, Liverpool need to approach this deal with caution and weigh up their options before making a final decision.

Lucas Chevalier wants to leave Paris Saint-Germain, Liverpool could make a move

Having a decent goalkeeper is one of the most important things for any football team.

Even if you have one of the best teams in the world in terms of outfielders, if your goalkeeper is poor, they're more than likely going to let you down.

This was the case when Giorgi Mamardashvili played last season with fans demanding that a new 'keeper was signed.

Initially, the Georgian was expected to take over from the Brazilian but, thanks to how poorly he performed, that didn't end up being the case.

Mamardashvili's poor form led to fans wondering who their next goalkeeper could be with a fresh update from L'Equipe now making that more than clear.

"Lucas Chevalier is ready to leave Paris Saint-Germain this winter. But there are many conditions for a departure. PSG will notably have to find a replacement before considering letting him go," they wrote.

Lucas Chevalier would be an out of the box signing for Liverpool

When Chevalier was brought to PSG by Luis Enrique, fans, pundits and journalists all thought that the Frenchman was destined to become their first choice.

Obviously he had some big shoes to fill after Gianluigi Donnarumma exited for Manchester City but, for Enrique's style of play, the Frenchman was the better option.

But, for one reason or another, the 25-year-old didn't hit the right notes and has been downgraded to their back-up by Matvey Safonov.

Neither of them are considered among the world's best but, Chevalier is almost certainly a better option for Liverpool than Mamardashvili would be.

Others such as Bart Verbruggen and Diogo Costa have also been linked with Liverpool but, since Chevalier actually wants to exit, a deal for him might be easier for Liverpool to agree on with PSG.

Nobody knows what the future has in store for any of Liverpool's first team squad but, if Chevalier is a player welcomed through the Anfield doors, the Reds will be in a decent place, even if he is replacing Alisson.

#1524. Motherwell vs Hibernian - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 26 Nov 2026 16:24

Motherwell and Hibernian will come together on Saturday evening for a Scottish Premiership clash at Fir Park.

The hosts are 11th in the Scottish Premiership table with 13 points, while the visitors are ninth with 14 points.

Motherwell initially recorded a positive start to the 2026-27 Scottish Premiership season, winning two and drawing two of their first four league games under new boss Alfred Johansson.

However, the Steelmen have subsequently recorded just one win in the following 10 league fixtures, alongside two draws and seven defeats.

That run included a particularly miserable six-game losing streak from September 5 to October 25, which was eventually ended by two draws and a win at the end of October and early November.

#1523. Opinion: Sensational player has officially announced himself as Liverpool's newest star

Liverpool have a new star. One player has officially announced himself as a key player with a fantastic performance.

Liverpool went into this season with a very imbalanced squad. It was one that required a lot from new head coach Andoni Iraola, essentially asking him to improve and experiment with players to get the most out of it.

Of course, that's largely the job of a head coach but it's rare that so much experimentation was necessary from a UEFA Champions League side that won the Premier League two seasons ago. But that's what Liverpool offered Iraola after two transfer windows that tore up large portions of the team.

No defensive midfielders, no recognised right-back, four left-wingers, no right-wingers, and one fit centre-forward. Hardly a 'win now' group of players. Iraola, though, has worked some real magic.

And that includes solving the defensive midfielder problem. At least for now.

The midfielder problem was a surprise one. We fully expected Liverpool to invest in the middle of the pitch over the summer but they simply ignored the issue. Even more bizarre was a decision to sell Curtis Jones without any sort of replacement.

It left Iraola short but it's a problem he appears to have fixed. Trey Nyoni has stepped up incredibly well, moving from a mere youth player who hoped for minutes to a genuine starting threat in the span of just a few months.

Wednesday night, though, felt like an announcement of sorts. Nyoni started away from home in the UEFA Champions League and thrived, holding down the midfield against a rampant Club Brugge.

Liverpool’s clean sheet made them the first team to hold out against Brugge for a very, very long time. The first team to beat Brugge in months, too.

Nyoni played his part. He wasn’t necessarily a defensive force by the way he won tackles here, it was more about his efforts on the ball to keep Liverpool ticking over.

92 per cent pass completion away from home in the Champions League is fantastic. It’s even more fantastic that he did it while completing 11 line-breaking passes - this wasn’t a case of Nyoni simply picking the simple ball every time.

That 11 was the third-highest figure in the match and second-highest for Liverpool (Jeremy Jacquet had 13). It’s exactly the kind of midfield play that the Reds have been crying out for and doing it at a difficult ground in the premiere competition is just outstanding from a 19-year-old.

Nyoni is special and this felt like an announcement. Confirmation that he is a proper star player and one Liverpool can count on in major fixtures.

#1521. Man United are in the relegation zone on merit and will need all of Mauricio Pochettino's coaching powers to get them out of it - they are chronically short of form and have forgotten how to win, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026

As the fourth goal flew in and Anfield rejoiced once again, Mauricio Pochettino stood on the touchline with his arms folded and turned to the Manchester United bench with an air of resignation.

What can he do to improve this shambles of a team? What could anyone do? United could change their head coach every game, but without the tools to do the job, the result will be largely the same.

Chief executive Omar Berrada said in an interview during the week that United have improved since the summer, but who is he trying to kid? They are in the relegation zone on merit, and it will need all of Pochettino's coaching powers to get them out of it.

He emerged from the tunnel shortly before 4.30pm here dressed smartly in blue, and after greeting Andoni Iraola and his staff, spent a few moments gathering his thoughts while You'll Never Walk Alone echoed around Anfield.

The game plan was in tatters inside 13 minutes, though, as he watched United go two goals and one man down. There was much finger wagging from Pochettino when Leny Yoro was somewhat harshly sent off, but the decision was never going to be overturned and nor should it be used to mask another United debacle.

As the enormity of the task he has taken on dawned upon him in the second half, the Liverpool fans taunted: 'Poch is the wheel.'

Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Man United head coach ended in a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool

The manner of the display was a microcosm of why United are mired in the relegation zone

Pochettino made two changes to the line-up from Michael Carrick's last game in charge against Aston Villa, and the biggest of them backfired spectacularly.

Giving Matthijs de Ligt his Premier League start for more than a year against Liverpool at Anfield felt like a gamble as he replaced Harry Maguire in central defence.

'When I saw Matthijs de Ligt's name on the team-sheet I was absolutely stunned,' admitted former United defender Gary Neville on Sky Sports, citing De Ligt's performance on his only start since last November in the Champions League defeat by Como in October.

However, the Dutchman was at fault for misreading the situation that led to Yoro being sent off in the eighth minute for the foul on Alexander Isak that saw Dominik Szoboszlai fire Liverpool ahead from a free-kick, and was the nearest United defender to Florian Wirtz when he hooked in the second shortly afterwards.

De Ligt got away with falling flat on his face and allowing Isak a free run on goal just after the hour mark, but couldn't stop Bradley Barcola's cross going through his legs when Rio Ngumoha scored the third shortly afterwards.

The nightmare was complete when his ill-judged pass to Joshua Zirkzee let in Liverpool for Victor Munoz to make it 4-0.

Pochettino's other change was to leave out Amad Diallo - who has claimed a couple of memorable goals against Liverpool but hasn't scored for United in nearly a year - and play Patrick Dorgu on the left.

Dorgu returned from injury to head a dramatic late equaliser in Carrick's final game in charge, but he was deemed to be unfit for duty by Denmark who sent him home during the international break.

He started on the left side of attack but switched to left-back when Yoro was sent off and Pochettino reshuffled what is statistically the worst defence in Europe as he tried to avoid a bloodbath.

Matthijs de Ligt (right) endured a nightmare game at centre-back as United were thumped

Pochettino's response to a horror start was to send on Maguire for Bryan Mbeumo, his best attacker, to provide extra protection for De Ligt.

Having started the game in United's familiar 4-2-3-1 formation, he switched to 5-3-1. Moving to a back-five when your team only has 10 men felt like damage limitation.

It needed some excellent saves from Senne Lammens - not to mention a crucial block by Maguire to send Isak's effort over the bar before half-time - to spare United from an embarrassing defeat on a par with the seven and five goal humiliations at the hands of Liverpool in recent years.

Even so, after seeing his team record a pitiful xG of 0.14 in a first half that saw United have one shot on target and four touches in the Liverpool box, he knew they had to pose more of an attacking threat if only to relieve the pressure on their defence.

Zirkzee replaced the anonymous Matheus Cunha at half-time in the hope that he could hold the ball up better, but the xG rose only marginally to 0.63 by the end compared to Liverpool's 4.38.

Pochettino sent on Mason Mount and Noussair Mazraoui for Youri Tielemans and Dorgu in the 65th minute, and they had only been on the pitch for a matter of seconds when Ngumoha got Liverpool's third.

Senne Lammens produced multiple save to prevent the scoreline from further embarrasment

There are so many problems piled up for Pochettino, it will be difficult to know where to start when he returns to his desk at Carrington on Monday ahead of this week's Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon in Portugal.

This is a team chronically short of form and confidence that has forgotten how to win. There are only so many changes he can make with the squad available until the January transfer window, so the Argentine is stuck with what he's got until then.

But United have simply got to stop giving up early goals. It was a problem that plagued Carrick against Atletico Madrid, Como, Roma and Villa, and any hope that Pochettino could stop the rot disappeared inside eight minutes here.

Yoro's red card was also United's fourth in the last eight games (and his second), which is another bad habit they will have to kick if Pochettino is going to turn this season from hell around.

#1520. Opinion: Richard Hughes' bargain deal has saved Liverpool's season

Liverpool finished the 2025-26 season rather poorly.

They were so bad that Arne Slot was actually relieved of his duties.

Admittedly, this came as a bit of a surprise to most people as fans thought that Fenway Sports Group were going to try and stick with the Dutchman for at least one more season.

Obviously, that didn't end up happening and in the end, Andoni Iraola took over and is currently leading the Reds to a fourth-place finish.

Their performances may have improved but, that doesn't mean that they should settle for fourth, especially since they spent over £150 million on new players in the summer.

Despite this, it's good that things seem to be going well with one of Richard Hughes' last deals potentially saving Liverpool's campaign.

Jeremy Jacquet was a bargain buy from Richard Hughes

When the £55 million fee for Jeremy Jacquet was first revealed, most people thought that Liverpool massively overspent on him.

The centre-back is only 20 years old and has had no experience of football outside of Ligue 1.

He was also playing for a Rennes team which weren't seen as one of France's best which led many to believe that he was just outperforming his teammates, rather than actually playing well.

However, since coming into Liverpool's starting XI, Jacquet has changed the minds of the doubters and has quickly entered the conversation as one of the Premier League's best-performing defenders.

The Frenchman has played an awful lot of football for Liverpool this term and has had a couple of different partners in the centre of defence.

But, every challenge he has faced has led to his skills improving which is why the Reds' season could have been saved by the youngster.

Liverpool would be a lot worse off without Jeremy Jacquet among their ranks

As mentioned, Jacquet is now being mentioned as one of the Premier League's best young defenders.

The way that he carries himself on the pitch and the way that he quickly rectifies any mistakes he makes is impressive.

On the ball, he's extremely confident and, if needed, he can ping a pass across the pitch.

Without Jacquet among their ranks, Liverpool would have to start with Joe Gomez or Ronald Araujo in the centre of their defence.

And, while Araujo has played as a centre-back for the Reds this season, if he was used there in each and every game, their right-back situation would be very dicey.

Jeremie Frimpong isn't up to scratch and, with Conor Bradley still side-lined due to injury, someone such as Dominik Szoboszlai or Gomez would have to be played out of position to cover that role.

So, the fact that Jacquet is a Liverpool player is a massive help to them and is likely one of the main reasons why they're only seven points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

#1514. GdS: ‘EuroMilan: the final call’ – four necessities to get the European campaign back on track

AC Milan have made a false start in their Europa League campaign, and they are running out of chances to put things right.

After losing three of their first four games in Europe, this morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) writes that Milan must win away from home against Olympiacos to keep their hopes of reaching the round of 16 alive.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In Athens, Ruben Amorim will put out his strongest side to try and do exactly that. Christian Pulisic and Diego Moreira will operate on the flanks, while Omari Hutchinson is set to feature behind Gonçalo Ramos. They have broken the mission down into four parts.

In Europe – a stage where Milan traditionally feel at home – the team has only truly looked comfortable against RB Salzburg, where they cruised past their opponents. Bournemouth proved to have too much, and even at San Siro Benfica and Ferencváros emerged with wins.

One fact remains: while Milan are flying in the league, their attempt to take off in Europe never quite got off the ground. There is a gap that must be bridged: the distance between the Milan seen in European competition and the side so highly regarded in the league.

This extends to individual performances: the highly-praised Rabiot and Moreira have been instrumental in pushing Milan toward the Champions League spots domestically, yet they have yet to carry that form into Europe.

The Frenchman has tallied 5 goals and 6 assists in Serie A, but only one assist in European play. The Belgian has 4 goals and 4 assists in the league, yet has failed to produce a decisive moment in continental competition. It is time to bring that form onto the continent.

In the league, we see a Milan that never leaves its strongest players on the sidelines. In the wake of the defeat to Ferencváros – which followed a victory in the derby – Amorim remarked: “Perhaps we aren’t ready to be competitive every three days.” Now, the team must prove him wrong.

Hopes for European qualification depend on climbing from the current 28th-place position, which requires goals. Those goals are expected to come from Gonçalo Ramos. In the Rossoneri’s only European victory so far, he did get on the scoresheet, but it was the final one in a 4-0 rout.

So, it could hardly be described as a decisive goal. That is exactly the kind of contribution needed this evening at the Karaiskakis Stadium, where the Diavolo will fight for a chance to rejoin the pack within reach of the play-off spots at the very least.

Ramos is the man for the job: he is the current No.9, he has just returned to scoring in the league after a drought, and with January approaching, there is the prospect of a fresh influx of goals. Following the celebration against Frosinone, Amorim hopes for a repeat in Athens.

The narrative that he is a ‘team-oriented’ striker holds water and has served as a valid defence against those questioning his lack of goals given he ranks second in the league for successful hold-up plays, third for flick-ons, and boasts impressive statistics in ball recovery and defensive actions.

While these figures highlight his excellent team contribution, the financial investment of over €70m is also significant. From a forward who is a two-time European champion, it is only fair to expect goals that truly make the difference.

Another objective for this European night is to prove the team’s stature even without the immense Luke Modric, who is sidelined due to injury. Ardon Jashari will take his place, making Milan less focused on possession and more on aggression.

The style of play will mirror that of their opponents: individual duels – and, by extension, the intensity and approach to the match – will be more decisive than ever. While the squad has often been heavily rotated in previous European fixtures, this time it will feature the strongest XI available.

Jashari’s dynamism will need to come to the fore. Without Luka’s class and command of the tempo, the team’s playmaking dynamic shifts. Milan must turn this into an action-packed encounter, full of constant twists and turns, to avoid being sidelined by their opponents.

Assisting in this effort will be Rabiot and Pulisic, the latter acting as a vital link between the midfield and the attack. The required intensity should translate into a greater presence in the opposition’s hal. Ideally, right inside the penalty area.

Paradoxically, following the celebration against Frosinone, Amorim was the least satisfied: he had wanted more sustained pressure near or inside the opponent’s box. Now, necessity dictates this approach: a controlled game must give way to an all-out assault.

Beyond Jashari – who is expected to provide more running and pressing – Moreira remains another key weapon, thanks to his surging runs down the flanks. Meanwhile, Alphadjo Cisse and Hutchinson serve as options Amorim can call upon during the match should the team need a spark.

Climbing the standings is a must. Milan may sit fourth in the league, but they cannot afford to be twenty-eighth in the Europa League table. Moving up won’t be easy: the Greeks remain unbeaten (three wins and a draw) and have conceded only one goal.

It is the joint-best defensive record in the UEL (along with Bayer Leverkusen). That is hardly an encouraging statistic for a Milan side that must score in order to win, because as things stand total elimination is on the cards.

This would be a disgrace for a club aiming to reclaim its place as a major player on the international stage. There is still time to recover, however. Looking at the last two editions, 14 points (2024-25) and 16 points (2025-26) were enough to get into the top eight. Milan are on three, with 12 up for grabs.

So, Amorim’s side could even aim for direct qualification. However, a complete turnaround would be needed. So, the play-offs are more realistic, and – based on the figures from the last two editions – 9 or 10 points would be required in this case.

Milan would thus need to obtain another six or seven points from their upcoming matches against Sunderland (at home), Levski Sofia (away), and Ararat-Armenia (at San Siro). By no means an easy task, however.

#1513. Opinion: Liverpool given green light to sign £46m sensation

Liverpool have been linked with a lot of players over the last few years.

Over £600 million has been spent on them and, more change is still needed.

Obviously, this isn't the outcome that the Anfield outfit will have wanted but, it's the hand that they've seemingly been dealt.

All of their rivals are constantly looking for ways to upgrade their team and, the more that they manage to do this, the better they become and the more difficult they are to beat.

Fans expected Liverpool to be competing for silverware this term but, now that feels like it all rests on their transfer plans with the club now being handed a green light to sign one of their targets.

Barcelona want to sign Ayden Heaven which could give Liverpool the green light to sign Ronald Araujo

One of the main positions that Liverpool needed to upgrade in the 2026-27 transfer window was their defence.

Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate both exited Anfield for free and, the performances of Jeremie Frimpong and Conor Bradley were shoddy.

Throw in the fact that Bradley managed to suffer yet another long-term injury and, Liverpool were left with a bit-part defence.

That's why Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo were brought in.

Nobody knew how each defender would perform due to their lack of Premier League experience but, to the surprise of many, they've been two of the Reds' best players.

But, because Araujo is only on a season-long loan, his future is still undecided or, it was until this fresh update from BBC Sport.

"Fulham and Barcelona are among the clubs to have expressed an interest in Heaven, with both having tried to sign him when he decided to leave Arsenal," they wrote.

"The England U20s defender's preference is believed to be a loan move, though he would also entertain permanent offers.

"At United he has largely been used as a back-up option and, after enjoying a run in the team under former manager Ruben Amorim, he lost his place under Michael Carrick. He returned to the side only after an injury crisis hit the club last season.

"Heaven is also capable of playing at left-back and in midfield, but does not expect to be trusted as a regular starter amid the instability at Old Trafford, with the club 19th in the league.

"He is under contract until 2029 in a deal that includes an option for an extra year."

Ayden Heaven joining Barcelona could force Barcelona to sell Ronald Araujo

Araujo's versatility is one of the best things about him.

The defender can be comfortably used as a centre-back or a right-back with Iraola using him in both positions this term.

Indeed, the Uruguayan's injury history is a bit of a worry but, touch wood, he's managed to keep fit while playing for Liverpool so far.

As mentioned, Araujo's future isn't set in stone yet but, if Barca manage to sign Heaven from Manchester United, it feels like Araujo would fall further down Hansi Flick's plans.

This could mean that the La Liga giants are willing to negotiate a cheaper deal for the centre-back which, judging by the recent developments from Liverpool, is exactly what they want.

Here's hoping that a deal can be reached soon and that Barcelona find a successor for their captain soon.

#1511. I was in the room with Newcastle bosses as they were grilled by fans on Matthias Jaissle, their January transfer plans and the new stadium - here's what they had to say, and my verdict: CRAIG HOPE

Published: 07:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 10:59 EST, 24 November 2026

Newcastle United’s hierarchy addressed supporters at a ‘United We Stand’ event in the shadow of St James’ Park this week.

Chief executive David Hopkinson, sporting director Ross Wilson, chief financial officer Simon Capper and chief operating officer Brad Miller were on stage discussing head coach Matthias Jaissle, transfers and the prospect of a new stadium.

Our chief football reporter, Craig Hope, was also in the room, and here is his rundown of all the key topics…

‘Arsenal (2-2 draw) felt like a real step forward in the second-half, you felt the energy change in the stadium. But as positive as it was, the biggest feeling we have right now is one of frustration, because the first half wasn't good.

‘We have seen that a few times already this season. An outstanding first half against Hull and a difficult second half. Maybe at Tottenham, 90 minutes straight, really good. Crystal Palace, the second-half very good, first half not.

‘So we're definitely trying to find consistency and Saturday was positive. The team felt like they owed that performance to the fans in the second-half. The frustration is that we didn't see that for 90 minutes.’

Sporting director Ross Wilson and chief executive David Hopkinson were among the members of the Newcastle hierarchy to answer questions from fans on Monday

The discussion came in the wake of a promising Saturday performance against Arsenal

HOPE: It would have been easy for Wilson to say, ‘Wasn’t Saturday great? We build from here’. Instead, he gave an honest assessment of where the team is at - because progress cannot really be achieved by playing well for 45 minutes here and there. It felt like a little warning shot, and a fair one.

‘I want to be really clear (about Vision 2030). I think sometimes it has been misreported as, “Oh, I’m guaranteeing we're going to win by 2030”. No, what I have is guaranteed is that we're in the conversation.

‘(Re 2.0) We set up with a plan that was very coherent of what we wanted to accomplish this summer. Not incremental change, but necessary and significant change. We lost three players who were important contributors to the past season.

‘We set out on a direction under Ross' leadership where we would have a different set of expectations that recognised financial reality. We articulated a vision for the squad here that would be organised around some young talent, who we expect to grow here.

‘So I’m delighted with the job Ross did. We executed that strategy superbly. Not everything that we set out to do was accomplished. We went hard on Johan Manzambi and didn't succeed. We went hard on Victor Munoz, didn't succeed, despite thinking we were going to land both of those at one point. But also had successes that we had not anticipated.’

HOPE: Wilson also spoke about the strategy of bringing down the squad’s average age, and there appeared to be no panic or concern over the so-far indifferent impact of summer additions. It has been noted by many that on Saturday, in the second half, no new signings were involved apart from goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek. For me, you cannot judge players over three months (look at Lewis Hall) but the big price tags attached to some of the young arrivals has raised expectation. Jaissle and the hierarchy need the likes of Matias Fernandez-Pardo, in particular, to start impacting, if questions over summer business are to quieten.

’In simple terms, the club had maxed out its credit card in the first few years under the new ownership. We had complied with PSR but it had been incredibly tight, and that forced us to sell at an undervalued price people like Elliot Anderson. We didn’t want to and we didn't want to be there again.

‘So we had to do something differently. The good news is that the Premier League has changed their rules so that there's a bit more headroom now. We’re comfortably within those and we're also comfortably within what we've agreed with UEFA (Newcastle were fined earlier this year). So we're in a really good place. That's the work that David and Ross had talked about in terms of 2.0.

‘That allows us to actually continue to invest and trade. It means that we've got no imperative to sell somebody in January. And it gives us the ability, depending on where we are in the league at the end of this season, to invest again at a proportionate level, depending on what European competition you qualify for.’

HOPE: The message was clear - there is scope to spend in January and next summer. Newcastle should use that to target goals in the New Year.

New Magpies coach Mathias Jaissle was also under the microscope in the shadow of St James' Park

‘Eddie Howe was a workaholic and he put his heart and soul into the job. So we needed someone who would work hard and the players would not notice a drop off. Matthias works incredibly hard.

‘Eddie was also outstanding on the grass, an elite coach. Again, our players couldn't feel, “Eddie’s gone and they've got another guy who doesn't coach”. Matthias is an expert, elite coach.

‘From a transfer perspective, the head coach at Newcastle always has the final say in any player who comes in. Matthias puts a lot of effort into that - convincing players and making sure they're the right character fit for him. He’s thrown himself into all things Newcastle and we enjoy working with him a lot.’

‘Matthias is a clear winner. And you know winners, they win over time. I have a high, high conviction we're going to win under his leadership. I don't think I've ever had the conviction more that we're going to win together than I do right now.’

HOPE: It is a bold statement from Hopkinson on the back of one win in seven, but the support for Jaissle is clear. He will (and should) be given time, despite an inconsistent start that has included a couple of horror shows. It was also interesting to note Wilson’s reference to Jaissle’s heavy involvement in transfers, on the back of a week in which the head coach let it be known he wanted more control over transfers.

‘This decision is going to last forever. It will outlast our lifetime. It’s that enormity that means we are taking a little bit of time now.

‘Is it going to allow us to compete with the top clubs? Are we going to be able to do it from a financial perspective? Is it going to be transformative for all of our fans, the city and for the region? For all of those reasons, we are very purposely taking our time. But whether we stay at St James’ Park or move, it will be absolutely fantastic.’

Newcastle continue to mull key decisions on the renovation of their stadium in a bid to unlock new revenue for the club

‘We need it (larger stadium) for the revenue a new stadium will unlock. This is a generational decision and will define the next era of this club. It’s going to be really expensive. We’re advancing significantly into clearly defined options. This is a project with global significance.

‘We've spent a lot of time with New York bankers recently thinking through how we might do this and what options we can consider. I can assure you we're working on this every day. I hope we will have something concrete to share with you soon.’

HOPE: There was ‘no update’ but the subtext of the discussion was very definitely geared towards a new stadium. I understand this is the direction of travel now, and Hopkinson confirming our story from last week about the high-level talks with Goldman Sachs over how to finance a new stadium demonstrates how advanced the project is.

Overall, the tone of the night was one of ‘we have a plan, stick with us’. It was very different 12 months ago, when the mood in the room was one of huge optimism and excitement at the unveiling of a new executive team ahead of a Champions League campaign.

Now, it feels like all involved - supporters and those on the inside - realise that this part of the journey will not be easy. That was reflected in the message conveyed.

#1510. This is going to hurt: Liverpool reportedly preparing for massive departure

Liverpool are preparing for a massive departure that will change the side dramatically. This one is going to hurt.

Liverpool have said goodbye to a series of legends over the last few years. It really started in 2021 when Gini Wijnaldum left for Paris Saint-Germain and then Sadio Mane decided to leave for Bayern Munich a year later. Slowly but surely, Jürgen Klopp's team has disappeared.

Jordan Henderson, Roberto Firmino and Fabinho left in 2023. Klopp himself left in 2024, as did Joel Matip and Thiago. 2025 was a big one - Trent Alexander-Arnold joined Real Madrid. Then things got even more heartbreaking in 2026 as Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate departed.

Salah's exit was arguably the most difficult of the lot. That was the biggest sign that things had moved on - the icon of Klopp's team deciding it was time to leave.

And now 2027 awaits and things are set to continue down the same path. The final stars of that great side have expiring contracts and it increasingly looks like it's time to say goodbye.

Liverpool are reportedly preparing the exit of Alisson Becker, whose contract will expire at the end of the campaign. Alisson's deal was due to end in 2026 but the Reds triggered an option to extend it by a year.

Juventus did try to get a deal done last summer regardless of that, offering a minimal fee to Liverpool. Nothing came of it, however, as no one at the Reds seemed keen to sell the Brazilian.

But Alisson may leave next year. Liverpool won't want him to go but offering a new contract to a goalkeeper with his injury history feels like a big risk. A risk they may not want to take if other options are available.

Of course, 'other options' of Alisson's calibre are few and far between. L'Equipe, though, understand that Liverpool have found one. They're eyeing Robin Risser of RC Lens, who was voted the best in Ligue 1 last season.

The 21-year-old is being discussed at Anfield internally as a potential option should Alisson leave. It's the first real sign we've had that the club are very much open to moving on from arguably their greatest-ever goalkeeper.

But we wonder if that could change because of Risser. There's intense competition for him and if he picks somewhere else, we imagine Liverpool will 'settle' for renewing Alisson's deal.

It's very much wait and see, then, but the Reds are certainly preparing for Alisson's exit.
